chant.letra:
[Leader]
How often do you read?
[Kids]
Daily! We read daily!

[Leader]
How often do you swim?
[Kids]
Twice a week! Twice!

[Leader]
How often is Oliver late?
[Kids]
Usually! Almost always!

[Leader]
And how often do we give up?
[Kids]
NEVER! Never, never!

[All]
Often, sometimes, once a weekend —
that's a habit, in the end!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
I always check the weather,
I usually get it wrong.
I often take the long way round
and sometimes take too long.

[Chorus]
Always, usually, often, sometimes,
never — say how much!
Once a day or twice a weekend,
a habit is a crutch or a touch!

[Verse 2]
Maya writes it down daily,
Ingrid never breaks a rule.
Diego sometimes writes at midnight
and is never late for school.

[Chorus]
Always, usually, often, sometimes,
never — say how much!
Once a day or twice a weekend,
a habit is a crutch or a touch!

[Bridge]
The word goes before the verb,
but after 'am', 'is', 'are' — that's the curve.

[Chorus]
Always, usually, often, sometimes,
never — say how much!
Once a day or twice a weekend,
a habit is a crutch or a touch!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What are you carrying?
[Kids]
The armchair! We're carrying the armchair!

[Leader]
What's in the box?
[Kids]
The lamp! The mirror! Careful!

[Leader]
Where are the curtains?
[Kids]
In the drawer! With the blanket!

[Leader]
And the sofa?
[Kids]
It's stuck! It's stuck in the door!

[All]
Carpet, pillow, box and lamp —
we are moving, up the ramp!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
We're taking down the curtains,
we're rolling up the carpet now.
The mirror's wrapped in blankets
and the lamp is on the prow.

[Chorus]
We're moving, we're moving,
everything is in a box!
Sofa, armchair, pillow, drawer —
and nothing fits and nothing locks!

[Verse 2]
The sofa's stuck inside the doorway
at exactly half past four.
Mr Vega measured twice
and it's still two centimetres more.

[Chorus]
We're moving, we're moving,
everything is in a box!
Sofa, armchair, pillow, drawer —
and nothing fits and nothing locks!

[Bridge]
Right now, this minute, as we speak:
that's the tense we're using this week.

[Chorus]
We're moving, we're moving,
everything is in a box!
Sofa, armchair, pillow, drawer —
and nothing fits and nothing locks!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What happened?
[Kids]
She broke her arm! On Monday!

[Leader]
What did they do?
[Kids]
An X-ray! They took an X-ray!

[Leader]
Who came?
[Kids]
Everybody! With cards and flowers!

[Leader]
And how was she?
[Kids]
Brave! Very brave!

[All]
Hospital, nurse and visit, week —
get better soon, that's all we seek!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
She broke her arm on Monday morning
on the ice outside the gate.
They took an X-ray straight away
and the nurse said we should wait.

[Chorus]
A week in hospital, cards and flowers,
visits every afternoon!
She was brave the whole time through —
and she'll get better soon!

[Verse 2]
On Tuesday Diego brought a story,
on Wednesday Oliver played.
By Friday she was walking
and by Sunday she had stayed too long, she said.

[Chorus]
A week in hospital, cards and flowers,
visits every afternoon!
She was brave the whole time through —
and she'll get better soon!

[Bridge]
Brave is not not being scared.
Brave is being scared and there.

[Chorus]
A week in hospital, cards and flowers,
visits every afternoon!
She was brave the whole time through —
and she'll get better soon!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
How does it start?
[Kids]
Greetings from the mountains!

[Leader]
What do you write?
[Kids]
What we saw! What we did!

[Leader]
What do you wish?
[Kids]
Wish you were here! Wish you were here!

[Leader]
And then?
[Kids]
Sign it! Stamp it! Send it!

[All]
Address, envelope and stamp —
Kili takes it, off he goes!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Greetings from a cold blue harbour,
we arrived on Saturday.
We walked the whole north headland
and we sent this on the way.

[Chorus]
Wish you were here, wish you were here!
Stamp and address, sign your name!
A postcard takes a fortnight
and it gets there just the same!

[Verse 2]
I sent one to my grandfather,
he received it late in June.
He kept it on the kitchen shelf
and read it every afternoon.

[Chorus]
Wish you were here, wish you were here!
Stamp and address, sign your name!
A postcard takes a fortnight
and it gets there just the same!

[Bridge — soft]
An envelope holds more than paper.
That's why we still send them.

[Chorus]
Wish you were here, wish you were here!
Stamp and address, sign your name!
A postcard takes a fortnight
and it gets there just the same!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
How about tennis?
[Kids]
Great idea! Let's play!

[Leader]
Shall we join the club?
[Kids]
Yes! Let's join today!

[Leader]
How about chess instead?
[Kids]
Boring! We prefer tennis!

[Leader]
Do we agree?
[Kids]
We agree! Maybe! We agree!

[All]
Suggest, prefer and join and play —
somebody has to say it first!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
How about a game of tennis?
Shall we join the club today?
Ingrid always makes the suggestion
and the rest of us say okay.

[Chorus]
How about it? Shall we? Let's!
Three good ways to ask a friend!
Agree or say you'd rather not —
the idea's not the end!

[Verse 2]
Maya says she'd prefer the pool,
Oliver says chess instead.
Diego says that both are boring
and then goes along, he said.

[Chorus]
How about it? Shall we? Let's!
Three good ways to ask a friend!
Agree or say you'd rather not —
the idea's not the end!

[Bridge]
Maybe is a real answer.
It just needs a time attached.

[Chorus]
How about it? Shall we? Let's!
Three good ways to ask a friend!
Agree or say you'd rather not —
the idea's not the end!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
The music!
[Kids]
Too loud! It's too loud!

[Leader]
The box!
[Kids]
Too heavy! We can't lift it!

[Leader]
The question!
[Kids]
Too difficult! Say it again!

[Leader]
And the light?
[Kids]
Not bright enough! Not enough!

[All]
Cheap or expensive, easy or hard —
turn the volume down a bit!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The music's far too loud tonight,
the room is far too small.
The box is much too heavy
and it isn't light at all.

[Chorus]
Too loud, too heavy, too expensive —
or it isn't cheap enough!
'Too' means more than what you want
and 'enough' means just enough!

[Verse 2]
The question isn't difficult,
it just isn't easy yet.
Turn the volume down a little
and you'll hear it, I would bet.

[Chorus]
Too loud, too heavy, too expensive —
or it isn't cheap enough!
'Too' means more than what you want
and 'enough' means just enough!

[Bridge]
'Very' isn't 'too'. Remember:
'very good' is good. 'Too good' is odd.

[Chorus]
Too loud, too heavy, too expensive —
or it isn't cheap enough!
'Too' means more than what you want
and 'enough' means just enough!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
When I'm happy…
[Kids]
I smile! I smile and I sing!

[Leader]
When I'm sad…
[Kids]
I tell somebody!

[Leader]
When I'm angry…
[Kids]
I breathe! I count to ten!

[Leader]
When I'm worried…
[Kids]
I ask for a hug!

[All]
Surprised and proud and cry and laugh —
every feeling has a path!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
When I'm happy I laugh too loudly,
when I'm proud I stand up straight.
When I'm surprised I say nothing
for a very long, long wait.

[Chorus]
When I'm sad I tell somebody,
when I'm angry I breathe slow.
A hug, a word, a bit of quiet —
and the feeling starts to go.

[Verse 2]
When I'm worried I make lists
of everything that could go wrong.
Then I cross out all the ones
that never came along.

[Chorus]
When I'm sad I tell somebody,
when I'm angry I breathe slow.
A hug, a word, a bit of quiet —
and the feeling starts to go.

[Bridge — soft]
Crying isn't losing.
It's just water finding a way.

[Chorus]
When I'm sad I tell somebody,
when I'm angry I breathe slow.
A hug, a word, a bit of quiet —
and the feeling starts to go.

36.unidad: Do you do it or make it?

chant.letra:
[Leader]
The bed — make or do?
[Kids]
MAKE! You make the bed!

[Leader]
Homework — make or do?
[Kids]
DO! You do your homework!

[Leader]
A cake?
[Kids]
MAKE! You make a cake!

[Leader]
The dishes?
[Kids]
DO! You do the dishes!

[All]
Make a mistake, do your best —
make friends, do sport, and skip the rest!

cancion.titulo: Make the Bed, Do Your Best
cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
You make a cake and make the bed,
you make a noise and make a friend.
You do the dishes, do the chores,
you do your homework in the end.

[Chorus]
Make or do? There is no rule,
you learn them one by one!
Make a mistake, then do your best —
and that is how it's done!

[Verse 2]
You do sport on a Tuesday,
you make a cake on Saturday.
You make a mistake on both of them
and do it anyway.

[Chorus]
Make or do? There is no rule,
you learn them one by one!
Make a mistake, then do your best —
and that is how it's done!

[Bridge]
You make the thing that wasn't there.
You do the thing that's on the list.

[Chorus]
Make or do? There is no rule,
you learn them one by one!
Make a mistake, then do your best —
and that is how it's done!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What do you enjoy?
[Kids]
Cooking! I enjoy cooking!

[Leader]
What do you love?
[Kids]
Dancing! I love dancing!

[Leader]
What do you like?
[Kids]
Painting! And photography!

[Leader]
And what do you collect?
[Kids]
Comics! Stones! Everything!

[All]
Chess and puzzle, board game, hobby —
after the '-ing' comes the fun!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
I enjoy cooking on a Sunday,
Maya loves photography.
Oliver likes dancing badly
and he does it publicly.

[Chorus]
I like, I love, I enjoy —
and then the verb takes '-ing'!
Chess and comics, board games, painting —
a hobby is a quiet thing!

[Verse 2]
Diego collects old newspapers,
Ingrid collects maps.
A puzzle on a rainy evening
closes up the gaps.

[Chorus]
I like, I love, I enjoy —
and then the verb takes '-ing'!
Chess and comics, board games, painting —
a hobby is a quiet thing!

[Bridge]
A hobby isn't wasting time.
It's the part of time that's yours.

[Chorus]
I like, I love, I enjoy —
and then the verb takes '-ing'!
Chess and comics, board games, painting —
a hobby is a quiet thing!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What's on this channel?
[Kids]
A documentary! About the ice!

[Leader]
And this one?
[Kids]
A cartoon! We've seen it twice!

[Leader]
Who asks the questions?
[Kids]
The presenter! And Diego!

[Leader]
And who watches?
[Kids]
The audience! That's us!

[All]
Camera, video, programme, screen —
interview and in between!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The camera's on, the light is red,
the presenter counts to one.
Diego holds the microphone
and the interview's begun.

[Chorus]
On the screen, on the channel,
programme, cartoon, documentary!
Honestly, I mostly like
the ones that teach me something new!

[Verse 2]
The audience is only twelve,
the video is short.
But somebody in another town
will watch this whole report.

[Chorus]
On the screen, on the channel,
programme, cartoon, documentary!
Honestly, I mostly like
the ones that teach me something new!

[Bridge]
A screen is not a window.
Somebody chose what's in it.

[Chorus]
On the screen, on the channel,
programme, cartoon, documentary!
Honestly, I mostly like
the ones that teach me something new!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What did they take?
[Kids]
A map! A ship! And courage!

[Leader]
Where did they go?
[Kids]
To the pole! Over the mountain!

[Leader]
What did they discover?
[Kids]
A way! A way that no one knew!

[Leader]
Did they all return?
[Kids]
Not all of them. Not all.

[All]
Explorer, journey, brave and history —
somebody went there first!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
They left the harbour in October
with a ship and half a map.
They discovered that the mountain
had a pass behind the gap.

[Chorus]
Somebody went first —
and the journey wasn't planned!
Explorer, ship and pole and map,
and history in their hand!

[Verse 2]
Some returned in June and told it,
some returned and told it wrong.
Some did not return at all
and their names are in this song.

[Chorus]
Somebody went first —
and the journey wasn't planned!
Explorer, ship and pole and map,
and history in their hand!

[Bridge]
Brave is not the same as safe.
They knew that when they signed.

[Chorus]
Somebody went first —
and the journey wasn't planned!
Explorer, ship and pole and map,
and history in their hand!

40.gramatica: superlatives: the best, the biggest, the most...

chant.letra:
[Leader]
The best day?
[Kids]
Ever! The best day ever!

[Leader]
The biggest wave?
[Kids]
Ever! The biggest ever!

[Leader]
The funniest moment?
[Kids]
When Kili landed in the soup!

[Leader]
And the worst?
[Kids]
We've forgotten it already!

[All]
Smallest, most beautiful, most exciting —
one memory and it's still bright!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
It was the biggest sky I've seen,
the smallest boat we'd ever had.
The most exciting hour of the year
and honestly not bad.

[Chorus]
The best day ever, the funniest moment,
the most beautiful light of all!
One memory is worth a hundred —
and this one won't get small!

[Verse 2]
It wasn't the worst day either,
though the rain came in at three.
The worst days make the best ones
easier to see.

[Chorus]
The best day ever, the funniest moment,
the most beautiful light of all!
One memory is worth a hundred —
and this one won't get small!

[Bridge]
Short words take '-est'. Long ones take 'most'.
That's the rule, and that's the most.

[Chorus]
The best day ever, the funniest moment,
the most beautiful light of all!
One memory is worth a hundred —
and this one won't get small!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
The square or the market — which is older?
[Kids]
The square! Much older!

[Leader]
The street or the motorway — which is wider?
[Kids]
The motorway! Much wider!

[Leader]
Morning or evening — which is noisier?
[Kids]
Morning! Much noisier!

[Leader]
And Sunday?
[Kids]
More peaceful! And more empty!

[All]
Modern, ancient, narrow, crowded —
old and new, the same town!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The square is older than the market,
the market's noisier than the square.
The new streets are much wider
and the old ones don't compare.

[Chorus]
Older than, newer than,
noisier and more peaceful too!
Crowded, empty, narrow, modern —
one town, and it's old and new!

[Verse 2]
The ancient wall is still standing
where the modern school begins.
The town is both at once
and neither of them wins.

[Chorus]
Older than, newer than,
noisier and more peaceful too!
Crowded, empty, narrow, modern —
one town, and it's old and new!

[Bridge]
Short words: add '-er'. Long ones: 'more'.
'Peaceful' takes 'more' — that's the law.

[Chorus]
Older than, newer than,
noisier and more peaceful too!
Crowded, empty, narrow, modern —
one town, and it's old and new!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
The phone!
[Kids]
It's ringing! Answer it!

[Leader]
Who's speaking?
[Kids]
It's Diego! It's Diego!

[Leader]
Could I speak to Maya?
[Kids]
Hold on! Hold on a moment!

[Leader]
Is she there?
[Kids]
She's busy! Try later!

[All]
Wrong number, message, mobile, voice —
call again — you have a choice!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The mobile rings at half past eight,
I answer and I say hello.
Could I speak to Maya, please?
Hold on a moment — I'll go.

[Chorus]
Who's speaking? Hold on!
She's busy — could you call her later?
Wrong number, leave a message —
and the voice becomes a stranger!

[Verse 2]
A phone call is a small brave thing:
you can't see the other face.
You have to say who you are
and get straight to the case.

[Chorus]
Who's speaking? Hold on!
She's busy — could you call her later?
Wrong number, leave a message —
and the voice becomes a stranger!

[Bridge]
'Can' is fine. 'Could' is kinder.
One small word, one small reminder.

[Chorus]
Who's speaking? Hold on!
She's busy — could you call her later?
Wrong number, leave a message —
and the voice becomes a stranger!
